text: The first traffic light blew up in a police officer's face.
See, the city needed to stop drivers from crashing at busy intersections.
So they put up a signal with lights, to tell people when to stop and when to go.
The problem? The lights ran on gas, and a police officer had to work them by hand. One day the gas leaked, and it exploded, badly hurting the officer running it.
So the city took the lights down. Instead, a police officer stood in the middle of the intersection, directing traffic.
But standing in the middle of traffic all day was dangerous too.
Until 1912, when a police officer invented an electric traffic light, and cities started putting them back up.
The problem now? There were only two lights: red and green.
The light switched so suddenly that drivers could not stop in time.
So they added a yellow light, to warn you before the light turns red.
And that is the same traffic light we still use today.
Of course, to some people, it is still just a suggestion.
